We have performed a series of 3D relativistically-precise electromagnetic particle simulations to study the particle acceleration and magnetic field generation in relativistic collisionless shock fronts.
Weibel instabilities created in collisionless relativistic shocks are responsible for the particle acceleration and magnetic field generation in relativistic shocks.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of relativistic collisionless plasma shocks and their role in particle acceleration, magnetic field generation, and emission of radiation in relativistic astrophysical sources.
the physics of relativistic shocks in astrophysical environments and the acceleration of particles in such shocks.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Weibel and Buneman instabilities are responsible for particle acceleration in collisionless shocks and that the resulting jitter radiation is a possible mechanism for the observed complex time structure and spectrum evolution of γ-ray bursts.
relativistic collisionless shock fronts can generate strong small scale magnetic fields, which can accelerate charged particles and produce jitter emission.
Weibel instability generated small-scale magnetic field structures can accelerate particles and generate “jitter” type emission in the relativistic collisionless shock.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Weibel-instability generated magnetic field structure is appropriate to jitter radiation and not to synchroton radiation.
the Weibel-instability generated magnetic field is responsible for particle acceleration, generation of jitter radiation and for generation of magnetic fields in relativistic shocks.
the Weibel and other instabilities in relativistic collisionless jets are important in the acceleration of charged particles and the generation of magnetic fields in relativistic jets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Weibel mechanism for particle acceleration in collisionless shocks may be more important than previously thought, and that it can produce small scale magnetic fields which may be responsible for the jitter radiation observed in γ-ray burst afterglows.
the Weibel mechanism for magnetic field generation is very efficient in relativistic collisionless shock fronts.
the Weibel mechanism is the most likely mechanism for particle acceleration in relativistic collisionless shock fronts.
